summary: A history of Oregon's white supremacy, from 1840s black exclusion laws and a powerful 1920s Klan through Portland's neo-Nazi skinhead era to Joey Gibson's Patriot Prayer and its violent street rallies in 2017-2018.

evidence.note: Burnett leads the 1843 wagon train to Oregon, then passes the 1844 lash law against black residents
1920s Oregon Klan has highest per-capita membership; 1922 governor elected with Klan backing
Vanport built for black wartime shipyard workers, destroyed by the 1948 flood
Portland police left dead possums at black-owned restaurants; later a skinhead symbol
1988 skinhead murder of Mulugeta Seraw and the civil suit that bankrupted Tom Metzger
Joey Gibson biography and founding of Patriot Prayer after the 2016 RNC
2017 MAX train stabbings by Jeremy Christian, who had attended a Patriot Prayer rally
2018 rallies, police response and skull fracture; story ends at the November 2018 rally

notes: Two-part story: part 1 is Oregon's racist history, part 2 is Patriot Prayer, so both are primary; neither is a person or group, so roles are empty. Joey Gibson's birth year is uncertain in the transcript (aged 33 or 34) and left null. main_span ends null because Patriot Prayer was active at release. Scope set to local (Oregon / Portland area) though Vancouver, WA also features.
